chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Abū Ḥabīb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a slave from another man, while the seller had two slaves. He said to the buyer, 'Take them both, then choose one of them and return the other,' after having already received the payment. Then the buyer took them both, and one of them absconded from his possession.

He said: 'He should return the one that remains with him from the two, and take back half of the price that he paid from the seller, and go in search of the غلام. If he finds him, he may choose whichever of the two he wishes and return the other. But if he does not find him, then the remaining slave is to be between them: half of him belongs to the seller and half to the buyer.'

key_terms.عَبْدًا: a slave being purchased in the transaction
key_terms.فَأَبَقَ: he absconded or ran away from possession
key_terms.نِصْفَ ثَمَنِ: half of the purchase price to be reclaimed
key_terms.ٱلْبَائِعِ: the seller from whom the item was bought
key_terms.ٱلْغُلَامِ: the absconding slave sought after the incident
key_terms.ٱلْمُشْتَرِي: the buyer in the sale contract

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a buyer is told to choose one of two slaves, but one absconds before he makes his choice?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a sale in which the buyer was allowed to choose one of two slaves after taking possession of both, but one absconded before the choice was finalized. The Imam عليه السلام sets out how the loss and ownership are to be apportioned between seller and buyer, establishing a principle of shared liability when the designated item of sale has not yet been determined.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3543 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Habib, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as). He said:

"I asked him about a man who bought a slave from another man, and the seller had two slaves. The seller said to the buyer, 'Take them both, then choose one of them and return the other,' and he had already received the payment. The buyer took both slaves, but one of them escaped while in his possession.

Imam (as) said: 'He should return the one that is with him and reclaim half of the price he paid from the seller. Then, he may search for the escaped slave. If he finds him, he may choose either of them and return the other. But if he does not find him, then the slave that remains will be shared between them-half belonging to the seller and half to the buyer.'"
